transformation: Mapped coordinates by PubChem atom ID, copied numeric XYZ values and bond endpoint/order arrays without coordinate transforms, rounding, geometry inference or topology inference. center/bounds are separately derived framing metadata.
fidelity: One PubChem computed 3D conformer. Not an experimental structure, molecular dynamics, reaction path, electron density or atomic-radius measurement. Display sphere sizes, stick widths, offsets for multiple bonds and element colors are illustration choices.

hostContract.delivery: Declare the exact data binding before the model call. Prefix returned raw source deterministically before compilation; preserve raw source, data SHA-256, prelude and combined-source hash. No numeric array echo or scene repair.
hostContract.sourceCoordinates: DATA.atoms[].position are the uncentered source coordinates. For display, subtract DATA.center and apply one uniform scale; never change relative molecular geometry.

promptContext.name: Caffeine
promptContext.sharedInstructions: Author a real 3D ball-and-stick caffeine view from DATA. Use bounded loops and existing scene primitives; do not reconstruct or emit atom coordinate arrays. Respect atom IDs and exact listed bond orders. Apply one rigid group transform for any view rotation; do not invent atomic motion or chemistry. Keep the molecule readable against the dark scene, show its formula and a compact element legend, and identify it as a computed conformer. Element colors are palette tokens C=GREY_B,H=WHITE,N=BLUE,O=RED.

low.label: Heavy atoms, low mesh detail
low.bondSelection: Both endpoint IDs must be in DATA.selections.heavyAtomIds
low.instructions: Show all 14 heavy atoms and their 15 bonds using low-detail atom geometry. Explicitly label that hydrogens are omitted. Preserve double-bond order as a visual bond convention.

high.label: All atoms, higher mesh detail
high.instructions: Show all 24 atoms including 10 hydrogens and all 25 bonds, with visibly smoother 3D atom geometry and double-bond depiction. Keep H atoms smaller as a display convention, preserve exact coordinate geometry, and use a modest continuous rigid rotation to reveal depth.
